details: The US Producer Price Index (PPI) for March came in below economists' expectations for both headline and core measures, easing some inflation concerns. This unexpected data spurred a relief rally in risk assets, including Bitcoin, which surged past $76,000. This move also notably turned MicroStrategy's substantial Bitcoin holdings profitable for the first time since late March. The broader cryptocurrency market capitalization saw an increase of approximately $110 billion within 24 hours following the report.
title: US March PPI Misses Forecasts, Fuels Bitcoin Rally to $76,000

details: The European Central Bank's (ECB) latest report indicates an improvement in current inflation conditions compared to last year but cautions about rising inflation risks, primarily driven by elevated energy prices due to ongoing Middle East tensions. This assessment has led traders to anticipate that significant rate cuts are unlikely, with some even pricing in the possibility of future rate increases if inflationary pressures persist. ECB chief economist Philip Lane has also reinforced this stance, warning that interest rates could still rise if inflation proves more persistent than expected.
title: ECB Flags Rising Inflation Risks, Unlikely to Cut Rates Soon

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has downgraded its global growth forecast to 3.1% and issued a warning about a potential worldwide recession. This outlook is attributed to the ongoing US-Iran conflict and the expectation that oil prices will remain above $100 per barrel until 2027. The IMF highlights that this precarious economic climate, coupled with already tightening liquidity, poses a significant detriment to digital assets.
title: IMF Warns of Recession Risk, Cuts Global Growth Forecast Over War and Oil

details: At its March 17-18, 2026 meeting, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decided to keep the federal funds target range unchanged at 3.50% to 3.75%. This decision signals a continued environment of selective liquidity and implies that markets will need to demonstrate strong performance to achieve upside. For cryptocurrencies, this means their performance remains closely tied to broader macroeconomic conditions, as tighter-for-longer monetary policy generally reduces investor appetite for riskier assets.
title: Fed Leaves Interest Rates Unchanged, Reinforces Tight Liquidity

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has expressed full support for the European Commission's initiative to centralize the oversight of large crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) under the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA). This proposed shift represents the most significant structural change since the Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation took effect, aiming to bolster financial stability. However, market participants interpret this move as bearish for the cryptocurrency market due to the anticipated increase in regulatory scrutiny.
title: ECB Supports Centralized EU Crypto Oversight Under ESMA
